UPSTREAM: media: mtk-vcodec: Remove VA from encoder frame buffers The encoder driver has no need to do any CPU access to the source frame buffers. Use a separate structure for holding DMA addresses and sizes for those and remove, so we do not end up introducing any erroneous dereferences of those VAs. This fixes DMA-buf import from exporters that do not provide contiguous kernel mappings, which includes the MTK DRM driver. BUG=b:123551776 TEST=Build Kukui image. Signed-off-by: Tomasz Figa <tfiga@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: Hans Verkuil <hverkuil-cisco@xs4all.nl> Signed-off-by: Mauro Carvalho Chehab <mchehab+samsung@kernel.org> (cherry picked from commit 8b8130f0c76abb422b5fd98aba401cd97e0b88b9) Signed-off-by: Alexandre Courbot <acourbot@chromium.org> Change-Id: I87c04c770eef33284fe8872a2edac9528531a426 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1442336 Commit-Ready: Alexandre Courbot <acourbot@chromium.org> Tested-by: Alexandre Courbot <acourbot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Tomasz Figa <tfiga@chromium.org>

test_lists: Add 'toolkit_config' payload component in RMA shim. Add a cros_payload component 'toolkit_config' to create some config files in factory toolkit. The file added to the payload is a dictionary in json format, and currently supports 'active_test_list' and 'override_test_list_constants' field, which are also dictionaries. 'active_test_list' sets the active test list, and 'override_test_list_constants' will override test list constants using the key-value pairs in the dictionary. { "active_test_list": { "id": "main" }, "override_test_list_constants": { "override_constant_1": 1, "override_constant_2": 2, ... } } To add a toolkit config to an RMA shim, place it in toolkit/ directory in a bundle, or use the '--toolkit_config' argument in `image_tool rma-create` command. BUG=chromium:910037, chromium:918096 TEST=manually create an RMA shim and install to DUT. CQ-DEPEND=CL:1417510 Change-Id: Ia7a863cf6d75d911d7b40182d6c31f261fd675a3 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1416218 Commit-Ready: Cheng-Han Yang <chenghan@chromium.org> Tested-by: Cheng-Han Yang <chenghan@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Wei-Han Chen <stimim@chromium.org>

FROMLIST: uvc: Avoid NULL pointer dereference at the end of streaming The UVC video driver converts the timestamp from hardware specific unit to one known by the kernel at the time when the buffer is dequeued. This is fine in general, but the streamoff operation consists of the following steps (among other things): 1. uvc_video_clock_cleanup --- the hardware clock sample array is released and the pointer to the array is set to NULL, 2. buffers in active state are returned to the user and 3. buf_finish callback is called on buffers that are prepared. buf_finish includes calling uvc_video_clock_update that accesses the hardware clock sample array. The above is serialised by a queue specific mutex. Address the problem by skipping the clock conversion if the hardware clock sample array is already released.
